****************************
* Cache command lines e.g. *
****************************


[ Inspecting a bundle's in-memory cache ]

    $ gina cache:stats <bundle> @<project_name>

    or for every bundle in the project

    $ gina cache:stats @<project_name>



[ Flushing a bundle's render/output cache ]

    $ gina cache:clear <bundle> @<project_name>

    or preview without removing anything (nothing is touched)

    $ gina cache:clear <bundle> @<project_name> --dry-run



[ Flushing every bundle in a project ]

    $ gina cache:clear @<project_name>



[ Evicting only what a given event invalidates ]

    $ gina cache:clear <bundle> @<project_name> --event=<event_name>

    or across every bundle in the project

    $ gina cache:clear @<project_name> --event=<event_name>



[ JSON output (for scripting) ]

    $ gina cache:clear <bundle> @<project_name> --format=json


Notes:
  - cache:clear flushes ONLY the rendered-output cache (static: HTML +
    data: JSON). Compiled templates and HTTP/2 sessions are never touched.
  - It runs two passes: an OFFLINE reclaim of the bundle's on-disk cache
    dirs (including orphaned prior-release dirs a redeploy left behind), plus
    an IN-HEAP flush of the running bundle via its admin endpoint. A bundle
    that is not running still gets its on-disk cache reclaimed offline.
  - --event evicts only the entries a route registered via its
    cache.invalidateOnEvents, instead of flushing the bundle. It is the
    IN-HEAP pass only: registrations live in the running bundle's heap, so a
    bundle that is not running has nothing to evict. The offline dir reclaim
    is skipped (it is bundle-wide and knows nothing about events); each entry
    that IS evicted still has its on-disk body removed with it. Use --event
    to invalidate ACROSS bundles — a controller's self.cache.invalidateByEvent()
    only reaches its own process.
  - The offline reclaim assumes the default cache root (<project_path>/cache).
    A bundle that overrides server.cache.path to a custom absolute path is
    flushed in-heap (via the running bundle) but its on-disk orphans are not
    auto-reclaimed.
